chunks: Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

A man bequeathed thirty dīnārs to the descendants of Fāṭimah عليها السلام. He said: Then the man brought it to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, and Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “Give it to a certain elder from the descendants of Fāṭimah عليها السلام,” and he was burdened with dependents and of limited means.

The man said to him: “The man only bequeathed it to the descendants of Fāṭimah.” So Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “It does not make a real difference among the descendants of Fāṭimah عليها السلام, whereas it does make a difference for this man, and he has dependents.”

key_terms.أَوْصَى: he made a bequest or testamentary instruction
key_terms.اِدْفَعْهَا: deliver it or hand it over
key_terms.ثَلَاثِينَ دِينَارًا: thirty dinars given as the specified bequeathed amount
key_terms.عِيَالٌ: dependents or family members under one’s care
key_terms.مُقِلًّا: one of limited wealth or means
key_terms.وُلْدِ فَاطِمَةَ: the descendants of Fāṭimah عليها السلام

ai.seo_question: How should a bequest for the descendants of Fāṭimah عليها السلام be distributed when one recipient is especially needy?
ai.summary: This hadith concerns a bequest made for the descendants of Fāṭimah عليها السلام and the Imam’s direction to give it to a needy elder among them. It shows practical judgment in applying a general bequest to the individual within that group who is most in need, especially one with dependents. The report reflects concern for both the intent of the bequest and the welfare of vulnerable family members.
